solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tree with a pole

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for with
taken as written
a boom is a spar or pole, as on a sailing boat

explanation.surface: A tree with a pole beside it, perhaps a flagpole or a tent pole propped against the trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: WABOOM is a South African tree of the protea family; a boom is the long pole along the foot of a sail.
explanation.definitionFit: The waboom is a protea native to South Africa, an example of a tree.

clue.text: Hooligan after fighting could be this?

definitions.text: Hooligan after fighting could be this?

indicators.note: after means the first piece named comes second in line

blocks.note: war is fighting
ned is Scottish slang for a young hooligan

explanation.surface: A hooligan who has been in a fight may well be cautioned by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a lout who has been brawling is likely to have been cautioned.
explanation.definitionFit: Warned means cautioned, the sort of reprimand a brawling lout would receive.

clue.text: Rendering corrupt couple of musical sections, I celebrate

blocks.note: two bars of music
taken as written
to sing is to celebrate, as in singing someone's praises

explanation.surface: A musician celebrates while ruining a couple of passages of a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To barbarise is to make crude or debased, especially language, so it is rendering something corrupt.

clue.text: Abstract style of old district

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a part of town is a district

explanation.surface: An abstract style of art associated with some old part of town.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is a 1960s abstract movement using optical illusions, so it is an abstract style.

clue.text: Sort me out — big windfall needed?

indicators.note: to sort something out is to put it back in a new order

blocks.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A broke speaker pleads that only a big win can fix their finances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; 'out' does the rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Motser is Australian slang for a large sum of money, especially a gambling win.

clue.text: More and more you'll see this Maori skirt

blocks.note: più is the Italian musical direction meaning more
the same musical term once again

explanation.surface: Someone promising that, the further you look, the more of a Maori skirt you will see.
explanation.walkthrough: Più appears in score markings such as più forte, more loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: A piupiu is a flax skirt worn in Maori dance and ceremony.

clue.text: Freshens up flowers with water finally poured in

indicators.note: finally means only the closing letter of the word is used
something poured in goes inside a container

blocks.note: pinks are garden flowers related to carnations
the last letter of water

explanation.surface: Someone revives a vase of flowers by pouring in some water.
explanation.definitionFit: To prink is to dress up or smarten oneself, so it means freshens up.

clue.text: Gay rarely getting heard

indicators.note: heard means the word is taken as it sounds when spoken

blocks.note: earning is getting money

explanation.surface: A gay person is seldom listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rarely' belongs to the definition: the word is a rare one.
explanation.definitionFit: Urning is a rare, dated term for a homosexual man, coined in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Wooden decoration from India artisan fashioned

indicators.note: fashioned means shaped into something new

blocks.note: I is India in the radio alphabet
the letters of artisan, rearranged

explanation.surface: An Indian craftsman fashions a piece of decorative woodwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Intarsia is a form of wood inlay making pictures from pieces of differently coloured wood.

clue.text: Lots of online groups offering advice to fisherman?

blocks.note: two words of tackle advice: employ your net rather than a rod

explanation.surface: Internet forums dispensing tips to anglers.
explanation.definitionFit: Usenet is the old worldwide system of internet discussion newsgroups.

clue.text: In speech girl favouring a rhetorical device

indicators.note: in speech means we judge the words by how they are spoken, not spelt

blocks.note: Anna is a girl, for means favouring, plus the a taken as written

explanation.surface: A speechmaker uses a girl's preference for a particular style as a rhetorical trick.
explanation.walkthrough: The final 'a' is shared: it is both the last bit of the sound-alike and the start of the definition's article, so the definition is read as 'rhetorical device'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaphora is the repetition of a word at the start of successive clauses, a classic rhetorical figure.

clue.text: Mostly support unusual rice diet as contribution to healthy living

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter
unusual means out of the normal order

blocks.note: to back is to support
the letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone largely backs an odd rice-only diet as good for the health.
explanation.definitionFit: A bactericide kills germs, so it promotes hygiene and helps keep people well.

clue.text: Break up resistance fighting with doom all around

indicators.note: all around means one word surrounds the others on every side

blocks.note: fate as one's doom or destiny
R is the physics symbol for resistance
soldiers in action are fighting

explanation.surface: A resistance movement's fighters, facing certain doom, are broken up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resistance' looks like the partisans of the surface, but it is just the electrical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: To fractionate is to separate a mixture into its parts, so it means to break up.

clue.text: Fabric that's fine for hanging up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: an eric was the blood-money fine for murder in old Irish law

explanation.surface: A cloth that is suitable for hanging as a curtain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanging' suggests drapes, but the eric was a fine paid in place of execution for killing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ciré is a glossy waxed fabric, usually satin or silk.

clue.text: Bishop grabbed by fascinating woman coming round in animal skin

indicators.note: coming round suggests turning about to face the other way
something grabbed is held inside the grip of something else

blocks.note: a siren is an alluring, fascinating woman
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop is seized by a seductress who comes round to him wearing an animal skin.
explanation.walkthrough: SIREN is turned round to NERIS, and B goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A nebris is the fawn skin worn by Bacchus and his followers in Greek art.

clue.text: Islander to become ill reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said out loud, not as it is written

blocks.note: to sicken is to become ill

explanation.surface: An island dweller is said to have fallen ill.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicani were an ancient people of Sicily, so a Sican is an inhabitant of that island.

clue.text: May I moan about people now being deprived of their forests?

definitions.text: people now being deprived of their forests

indicators.note: about suggests the letters are moved around

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: Someone asks permission to protest about a tribe losing its forests.
explanation.definitionFit: The Yanomami are an Amazonian tribe whose rainforest home is threatened by logging and mining.

clue.text: Part of England known to Scots

blocks.note: first meaning: a county in the south-east of England
second meaning: in Scots, the past participle of ken, to know

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a region familiar to Scottish visitors; 'to Scots' actually flags a Scots word meaning known.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the English county of Kent and is also the Scottish form of the participle meaning known.

clue.text: Fish landed ultimately on short vessel

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word before it
short means the word loses its final letter
on in an across clue means one piece follows the other

blocks.note: the last letter of landed
an artery is a blood vessel

explanation.surface: A fish is finally landed and put on a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a boat, but it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A darter is a small freshwater fish of the perch family that darts about.

clue.text: Most wise and godly person having a long time inside

indicators.note: inside means placed within the other piece

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
ages is a long time, as in 'it took ages'

explanation.surface: The wisest are those godly people who have lived a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage means wise, and this is its superlative form.

clue.text: According to nature, uncertain or doubtful

blocks.note: s.n. abbreviates Latin secundum naturam, according to nature
iffy is informal for uncertain

explanation.surface: Something natural that seems uncertain or open to doubt.
explanation.walkthrough: SN is a dictionary abbreviation for the Latin secundum naturam.
explanation.definitionFit: Sniffy can mean disdainful or sceptical, holding back approval, hence doubtful.

clue.text: Botanical bit left below stalk

indicators.note: below in a down clue puts the first piece named underneath

blocks.note: a stipe is a stalk, as of a mushroom
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A small part of a plant remains beneath the stem.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipel is a small stipule at the base of a leaflet, a tiny part of a plant.

clue.text: Enthusiast, little man being under this illusion

indicators.note: being under this in a down clue puts the second piece beneath the first

blocks.note: a fan is an enthusiast
Tom, as in Tom Thumb, a short name for a man

explanation.surface: A devoted fan and a little man both suffer the same delusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantom is a variant spelling of phantom, an apparition or illusion.

clue.text: German attendants could be greasy

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might form something else

blocks.note: the letters of this word

explanation.surface: Servants from Germany might be oily characters.
explanation.definitionFit: A yager, from German Jäger, is a huntsman or a liveried attendant to a German noble.

clue.text: Religious code of unorthodox maharishi? Not him, somehow

indicators.note: not him tells us to take those letters out
somehow says the remaining letters arrive in some unspecified new order
unorthodox means not following the usual order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: Asking whether a religious code belongs to some unconventional guru, and deciding it is not his.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove H, I and M from MAHARISHI, then rearrange the six letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharia is Islamic law, the religious legal code derived from the Koran.

clue.text: Shell, one covered in nasty spume

indicators.note: nasty suggests something mangled out of shape
covered in means wrapped inside something else

blocks.note: the letters of this word, rearranged
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A seashell, one of many, lies smothered in dirty sea foam.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepium is cuttlebone, the internal shell of the cuttlefish.

clue.text: Time off in German region half wasted

indicators.note: half wasted means one of two halves is thrown away

blocks.note: Holstein, the region of northern Germany

explanation.surface: A holiday in a German region where half the time is squandered.
explanation.walkthrough: Hols is British informal for holidays.
explanation.definitionFit: Hols is a casual British word for holidays, a period away from work or school.

clue.text: Sort of wooden local dignitary to put mum off

indicators.note: off means taken away and removed

blocks.note: an alderman is a senior member of a local council
ma is mother, mum

explanation.surface: A wooden town councillor who is rude to his mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldern is an archaic adjective meaning made of alder wood, one kind of wooden.

clue.text: Fencer's cry when repeatedly coming back

indicators.note: repeatedly says the same word is used twice in a row
coming back means travelling the other way, right to left

blocks.note: as means when, used twice

explanation.surface: A fencer shouts each time the opponent keeps coming back at them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sa sa is an exclamation once used by fencers when thrusting, a cry of attack.

clue.text: Leaves Arabia or just one of its countries

blocks.note: qat or khat is a shrub whose leaves are chewed as a stimulant
Ar is a dictionary abbreviation for Arabia

explanation.surface: Someone leaves Arabia, or perhaps just one of its nations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: the stimulant leaves of qat. 'Its' refers back to Arabia.
explanation.definitionFit: Qatar is a small Gulf state on the Arabian peninsula, one country among several.

clue.text: Organic compound, one to dig out

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to mine is to dig ore out of the ground

explanation.surface: An organic compound that someone has to excavate.
explanation.definitionFit: An imine is a chemical with a carbon-nitrogen double bond, a class of organic compound.

clue.text: Fellow in Highland attire keeping cold and unemotional

indicators.note: keeping means holding something safe inside

blocks.note: the tartan cloth a fellow in the Highlands wears over his shoulder
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A kilted Highlander stays cold and unmoved.
explanation.walkthrough: A plaid is the long tartan wrap of Scottish Highland dress; 'Fellow in' only sets the scene of someone wearing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid means calm and not easily stirred, so unemotional.

clue.text: Like a sort of belief — isn't it cheap somehow?

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come out in some new, unspecified order

blocks.note: the letters of these words, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone sniffy about a belief system wonders whether it is a bargain-basement creed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantheism is the belief that God is identical with the universe, so pantheistic describes that type of creed.

clue.text: Sacred travelling around about biblical city? I fought for that

indicators.note: travelling letters move about and settle in a new order
about here means turned round to face backwards
around means wrapped about something placed in the middle

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
Ur of the Chaldees, Abraham's home city in Genesis

explanation.surface: A traveller to a holy biblical city declares that it was the cause he fought for.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer speaking: 'that' is the sacred city of the surface, Jerusalem. The reversed city goes in after the first letter of the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader was a medieval soldier who fought to win the Holy Land, Jerusalem above all.

clue.text: Feature of test — learner has problem get round nailing it

indicators.note: to get round is to turn about and face the other way
nailing means fixing one piece firmly onto the next

blocks.note: L is a learner, as on L-plates
taken as written
a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A learner sitting an exam faces a problem but finds a way around it and nails it.
explanation.definitionFit: Litmus paper is the indicator that turns red or blue in the classic acid test, a key part of it.

clue.text: Fabric getting chaps in tangle? The opposite

indicators.note: in normally puts the first word inside, but the opposite reverses which word holds which

blocks.note: chaps are men
tangle and ore are both kinds of seaweed

explanation.surface: Cloth that tangles up the men who handle it, or the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The opposite' swaps the order: tangle goes inside chaps. Tangle is a kind of kelp, and ore is an old word for seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: Moreen is a stout ribbed cloth of wool or cotton used for curtains, a type of fabric.
